title: setup-secrets lockdown glob misses dotfiles (fail-open)
detail: The unprocessed-file lockdown enumerates secretsDir with `printf '%s\n' *` under `shopt -s nullglob` but no `dotglob`, so dotfiles are never chowned root: or chmod 0440. After the script finishes it deliberately sets secretsDir to 0751 (world-traversable), so a dotfile placed there by root/admin with a permissive umask (e.g. 0644) stays world-readable to all local users, bypassing the 'all other files accessible to root only' guarantee. Only root can write into secretsDir, hence low severity. Fix: add `shopt -s dotglob` to the enumeration.
impact: Accidental world-readable secret if an admin or tool drops a dotfile (e.g. `.env`, `.backup-pass`) into the secrets dir.

title: WireGuard preset binds lnd admin REST to 0.0.0.0, guarded only by a source-subnet firewall rule that is not interface-scoped
detail: With lndconnect enabled, `services.lnd.restAddress = "0.0.0.0"` exposes the macaroon-admin REST API on all interfaces. Protection is a single iptables accept rule matching `-s 10.10.0.0/24` in the shared nixos-fw chain (all interfaces). The default 10.10.0.0/24 is a plausible LAN subnet, so a same-LAN host can match the rule; macaroons still gate the API, so this is defense-in-depth loss, not direct compromise. Documented as deferred in docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md (with a breakage checklist) and noted for interface-scoping in commit 895c7b9. Recorded here so the deferral stays on the findings ledger.
impact: Admin REST API reachable beyond the WireGuard peer in subnet-collision or firewall-misconfiguration scenarios; TLS+macaroon remain as the only barriers.

title: docs/install.md instructs installing Nix 2.3.10 (2021, EOL) on the deploy machine
detail: The deploy-from machine setup pins the Nix 2.3.10 installer (GPG-verified, which is good) but 2.3.x is years past end of maintenance and predates fixes for multiple sandbox-escape CVEs (e.g. CVE-2024-27297 fixed-output-derivation sandbox escape, fixed in 2.20.4+). Anyone evaluating untrusted flakes on the deploy machine with this Nix is exposed. Fix: bump the documented installer to a supported release and re-pin the .asc fingerprint steps.
impact: Known-CVE Nix daemon on the deployer workstation; risk materializes when building untrusted expressions.

title: bitcoind preStart compares config with an unquoted RHS glob pattern
detail: `[[ ! -e $confFile || $cfg != $(cat $confFile) ]]` treats the existing bitcoin.conf content as a glob pattern. If the file contains pattern metacharacters (reachable via admin-set `extraConfig`), a false 'equal' skips the rewrite, leaving stale rpcauth HMACs after secret rotation and breaking dependent services until manual intervention. No privilege boundary is crossed (the file is owned by the bitcoin user, who can already edit it); availability/robustness only. Fix: quote the RHS — `[[ $cfg != "$(cat "$confFile")" ]]`.
impact: Config update silently skipped; rotated RPC credentials not propagated (service DoS, recoverable).

title: Public RPC whitelist retains getblockstats; docs demonstrate rpc.allowip 0.0.0.0/0
detail: The whitelist's stated bar is 'bounded CPU cost per call'. getblockstats computes per-block fee histograms over full blocks and is the heaviest call remaining (seconds of CPU on large blocks, parallelizable only up to rpcthreads). The public user is intended for local services, but docs/configuration.md explicitly shows `rpc.allowip = [ "0.0.0.0/0" ]`, and if a user follows that, getblockstats is the cheapest remaining CPU-DoS amplifier behind credentials. Mitigations: rpcwhitelistdefault=0 and per-user whitelists are correct. Suggest a one-line caveat in the docs snippet, or dropping getblockstats to a 'heavy' opt-in list.
impact: If a user exposes the public RPC user as documented, holders of those credentials get a low-amplification CPU DoS.

title: Root ExecStartPost reads admin.macaroon through a symlink-followable path in the lnd-owned datadir and exfiltrates the bytes to lnd's own REST endpoint
evidence:
script = nbLib.rootScript "lnd-create-macaroons" ''  # line 262; rootScript = "+${self.script name src}" (pkgs/lib.nix:88) — unsandboxed real root
  adminMacaroonHex=$(${pkgs.xxd}/bin/xxd -ps -u -c 99999 '${networkDir}/admin.macaroon')   # line 280: root opens an lnd-writable path, symlinks followed
  ${curl} \
    -H @<(printf 'Grpc-Metadata-macaroon: %s\n' "$adminMacaroonHex") \   # line 282: file bytes sent as an HTTP header to lnd's REST listener
    -X POST -d '{"permissions":[...]} ${restUrl}/macaroon | jq ... xxd -p -r > "$macaroonTmp"  # lines 283-286
attack_scenario: Attacker: the lnd service user, compromised via an lnd exploit (the exact adversary the script's own comment names at lines 265-274). Steps: (1) replace /var/lib/lnd/chain/bitcoin/<net>/admin.macaroon — inside the 0770 lnd:lnd datadir lnd fully controls — with a symlink to a root-only file, e.g. /etc/nix-bitcoin-secrets/backup-encryption-env, wg-server-private-key, /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key, or /etc/shadow; (2) trigger a service start (Restart=on-failure spaced over time, any deploy, any reboot — ExecStartPost re-runs on every start); (3) the '+'-prefixed script runs as unsandboxed root, xxd reads the target THROUGH the symlink, and the hex-encoded content is transmitted as the Grpc-Metadata-macaroon header of the POST to https://<restAddress>:<restPort>/v1/macaroon — the listener the compromised lnd itself owns and reads. One root-only file per start; iterate per restart. Payoff: root-only secret exfiltration the lnd user could never read directly — the backup passphrase decrypts backups that contain the whole secretsDir and /var/lib/tor (backups.nix filelist), the wg server key fronts the admin REST API, SSH host keys enable MITM of operator access.
impact: secrets (root-only secret exfiltration; chains toward funds via wg-key/backup-passphrase/onion-key reuse)
false_positive_risk: Could be wrong if: (1) the '+' prefix did not bypass sandboxing for ExecStartPost — systemd.exec(5) documents that it applies to all Exec* commands and runs them with full privileges, namespace and filesystem restrictions not applied; (2) networkDir/admin.macaroon were root-owned or not lnd-writable — it is not: tmpfiles creates /var/lib/lnd 0770 lnd:lnd and lndinit/lnd create networkDir as the lnd user; (3) lnd could not re-run ExecStartPost — it re-runs on every service start, and a compromised lnd controls its own failures. Confirm with a VM test: plant a symlink at admin.macaroon and observe the header bytes received on the REST port.
recommendation: De-privilege the read so root never dereferences an lnd-controlled path: read the macaroon as the service user (e.g. adminMacaroonHex=$(${runAsUser} lnd cat '${networkDir}/admin.macaroon' | ${pkgs.xxd}/bin/xxd -ps -u -c 99999)) — a symlink to a root-only file then fails closed because the lnd user cannot read it — or open with O_NOFOLLOW and fstat-verify a regular file before reading. The existing root-only staging + rename(2) write path is correct and needs no change.
